title: Perfection of proper direct image of a relatively flat single module
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be proper, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], and $F$ a finitely presented module flat over $f$. Supply independent derived localizations on $X$ and $S$ and the localized open sites of $S$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Then $Rf_*(F[0])$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is perfect on $S$ [def-pc-perfect-complex]. No chosen Cech complex or base-change comparison occurs in this assertion.

source.place: Tag 0B91(2), specialized proof of Tag 0A1H with E=O_X and G=F[0]

proof.text: Work locally on affine S=Spec A and express A as a filtered colimit of Noetherian rings. Spread out the finitely presented morphism and single module, enlarging the stage so the morphism is proper and the module relatively flat. This is the specialization E=O_X, G=F[0] of Noetherian approximation of the tensor data.

Apply the Noetherian perfect-direct-image theorem to O_X tensor F[0]. Proper coherence supplies bounded coherent cohomology; relative flatness supplies finite Tor dimension. Identify pullback of this direct image with the original one by relatively flat derived base change. Its pulled strictly perfect representatives give perfection locally on S. Glue the witnesses and transport across localization uniqueness to exactly the supplied source, base and open localizations. Empty schemes and zero modules use zero representatives.
